deed: צהל הקים בית חולים שדה לפליטים אלבנים שנמלטו מקוסובו
title: The IDF set up a field hospital for Kosovo refugees in Macedonia, and 12 babies were born there

trailer.text: In April 1999 a medical mission of the IDF, the Israeli army, left for Macedonia to care for refugees from Kosovo.
On April 4 the Israeli Cabinet decided to contribute a field hospital for two weeks.
Six IDF cargo airplanes took off with pieces of the hospital, and it was set up at the refugee camp in Stenkovec, north of Skopje.
During the mission twelve babies were born at the hospital, and an Albanian Muslim mother named her daughter Sara, a Jewish name, out of gratitude to the doctors.

stations.title: The war and the flight from Kosovo

paragraphs.text: On March 24, 1999, NATO began bombing Yugoslavia, a federation of Serbia and Montenegro.
In response, Yugoslav President Slobodan Milosevic accelerated the emptying of Kosovo.
90 percent of Kosovo's 2 million inhabitants had been Albanian.
Within days, Albanians were moving en masse south and southwest, into impoverished Macedonia and Albania.
In April 1999, more than 200,000 refugees were staying in Macedonia, a country of 2 million, and 400,000 refugees in Albania.
According to an article from April 22, 1999, approximately 700,000 Albanians from Kosovo were reportedly uprooted from their homes in the month before its publication.
The flow of refugees overwhelmed local authorities and international relief agencies, and they appealed for help.
The Israeli Foreign Ministry sent an emergency relief shipment of medicine, medical equipment, jackets and tents for Kosovo refugees.
On April 4, 1999, the Israeli Cabinet made a snap decision to contribute a field hospital for two weeks, at a cost of roughly $1.3 million.
Israel had regarded humanitarian aid to those in need as official policy since 1958, the year it created MASHAV in the Foreign Ministry.
Two officials from the Israeli Embassy in Athens were sent to Macedonia to lay the groundwork.
The next day, Macedonian officials advised them to set up the hospital at Stenkovec, 10 miles north of Skopje.
At that time the camp housed only 2,000 refugees, and the Israelis were puzzled by the choice.
Jacob Dayan was one of the two Israeli coordinators and the second most senior official at the embassy in Athens.
He said he had been promised 30,000 refugees within a week.
According to him, within two or three days there were already 30,000.
Six IDF cargo airplanes took off with pieces of the hospital, blankets and tents.
On April 6, 1999, the IDF medical mission left Israel, four days after the Foreign Ministry's relief shipment.
According to israeled.org, the mission numbered 70 people, including 12 physicians of various specialties, most of them veterans of other relief operations.
According to the Jewish Journal article, a contingent of 80 set up the hospital on April 6.
It included doctors, nurses and medics, some of them army staff and some reservists, and they worked without a break through the night.
At 14:00 the next day, April 7, the hospital opened its doors.
According to RFE/RL, it was erected in 20 hours, less than two days after Israel decided to send it.
Colonel Hezi Levi was the commander of the hospital.

Israel had already set up hospitals for Cambodian refugees in Thailand in 1979 and for Rwandan refugees in Goma, Zaire, in 1994, and sent a rescue team to Kenya after the terrorist attack on the U.S. Embassy in Nairobi.
According to the Israelis, the specialty in field hospitals was born of necessity, because of the many wars and terrorist attacks in the Jewish state's 51 years of existence.
Ron Maor, an army surgeon with 14 years of service who had already served in Nairobi, said that Israeli society knows how to improvise and be creative.
According to him, it does not need much bureaucracy to act urgently.
The hospital had room for 100 beds.
Each tent served a different purpose: emergency room, surgery, X-rays and laboratory.
According to RFE/RL, it had an emergency room, a ward for the elderly and a ward for newborns with incubators, a laboratory, an X-ray machine, an ultrasound machine and an equipped pharmacy.
According to israeled.org, the hospital could perform basic trauma, orthopedic and gynecological surgeries, and the emergency room could treat hundreds of patients a day.
According to the Jewish Journal article, the Israeli team treated about 200 patients a day, around the clock.
They included refugees brought by bus from 10 refugee camps in Macedonia.
According to RFE/RL on April 14, the hospital treated about 150 patients a day.
The compound stood on the western edge of the camp, and there was order and relative quiet in it compared with the noisy camp.
Colonel Levi told of an 80-year-old woman who came with abdominal pain.
The team diagnosed appendicitis and operated on her, and afterwards she sat in the sun.
According to the Israelis, they lacked medicine and facilities to treat chronic illnesses such as heart disease, epilepsy and diabetes.
The children's ward drew the most attention.
According to RFE/RL, by April 14 seven babies had been born at the hospital.
According to the Jewish Journal, by the Sunday before the article's publication the Israeli team had delivered 11 babies.
Over the whole mission, twelve babies were born at the hospital.
One of the babies was given a Jewish name by her mother, an Albanian Muslim: Sara Berisha.
The mother chose the name out of gratitude to the doctors.
Sara was delivered by medic Yael Goldman, aged 20.
On April 15, three-month-old twins arrived at the camp, suffering from severe malnutrition and a respiratory infection.
The twins were in critical condition, and Goldman cared for them in an Israeli army incubator.
It was her first mission abroad.
She said that Jews had been through much hatred and that it is difficult to see it happening to others, and so she felt she had to do something.
Israeli officials also organized activities for refugee children at the Brazda camp.
The Brazda transit camp was established in 1999 at the Stenkovec airfield, north of Skopje.
NATO set it up in response to some 50,000 Kosovars stranded in a muddy field on the border, at Blace.
British NATO soldiers erected the first 500 tents in one night.
They were meant for refugees who had been in the rain for days without shelter or food.
According to RFE/RL, on April 14 about 25,000 refugees were in the camp.
Every day busloads of hungry, traumatized Albanians arrived at the camp, and the food line always numbered hundreds.
It had no portable toilets, only holed wooden planks over pits.
Refugees interviewed by RFE/RL expressed satisfaction with the services the camp in Brazda provides, and complained mainly of a lack of showers and of boredom.
A 22-year-old economics student from Pristina complained bitterly that people in the camp were living "like animals".
Physician Dan Engelhard, a professor at Hadassah, expected that as temperatures rose, epidemics such as measles, polio and dysentery would break out.
According to him, Macedonian officials and relief agencies were slow to provide sanitation and immunization, and children were especially vulnerable.
Engelhard, a pediatrician and reservist, had already served in Israeli field hospitals for Cambodian refugees in Thailand and for Rwandan refugees in Goma, Zaire.
He said that Kosovo cannot be compared with the Holocaust, but that the pictures of Albanians forced into trains are reminiscent of it.
Ron Maor said the refugees were "luckier" than his grandparents in Poland and Hungary during the war, because the Albanians have an international effort to help them.
According to UNHCR, the refugees evacuated to Israel were mainly special medical cases who were treated initially in the Israeli field hospital in Brazda.
In an RFE/RL report of April 14, Col. Levy said that Israel had sent about 100 refugees to Israel by aircraft; according to UNHCR, the evacuation to Israel took place on Monday, April 12.
In his view, the camp would operate for at least a few weeks.
When the team returned to Israel, two refugees from Kosovo received permission to fly with it.
They received permission to join a group of 111 Albanian refugees that had arrived in Israel a week earlier, and flew to Israel together with the team on the return flight.

stations.title: The handover and the return home

paragraphs.text: The Israeli two-week mandate was about to expire, and the team was expected to leave on Thursday.
Members of the team said they wanted to remain at the site until replacement teams arrived from other countries.
The hospital postponed its return to Israel from Monday to Thursday.
A second medical facility, of the German Red Cross, was set up within a week after the Israeli hospital.
The Germans and a team that had arrived from Taiwan were to take over hospital care.
Joachim Gardemann, dean of the nursing school at the University of Applied Sciences Münster (FH Münster), said that it moved him, as a German, to work closely alongside the Israelis.
He called the Israelis "world champions" of army field hospitals, and proudly displayed a red Star of David pin he had received from them.
According to JTA, the medical team returned to Israel on Thursday, after a 17-day humanitarian mission at the Brazda camp, near the border with Kosovo.
According to JTA, the team treated some 1,500 Albanian refugees, 140 of whom were hospitalized.
According to israeled.org, the hospital treated more than 1,560 people over 16 days, and referred some patients to primary clinics established in and around the camp.
According to an article from April 22, 1999, Israel filled a critical void in Macedonia when it set up an army field hospital for refugees.

claims.quote: Macedonia, a nation of 2 million, now wheezes under the strain of more than 200,000 refugees, while Albania’s more than 3 million citizens, the poorest in Europe, cope with 400,000 refugees.

claims.text: גורמים ישראליים ארגנו פעילויות לילדי הפליטים במחנה ברזדה.
claims.quote: Israeli officials are organizing activities for young refugees at the Brazde refugee camp.

claims.text: חיילים בריטים של נאט"ו הקימו בלילה אחד את 500 האוהלים הראשונים במחנה, עבור פליטים שהיו ימים בגשם בלי מחסה ואוכל.
claims.quote: In just one night, British NATO soldiers already in the country erected the first 500 tents at Stenkovec, providing the first bit of civilization for refugees who had been out in the rain, without shelter or food, for many days.

claims.text: לפי RFE/RL ב-14 באפריל 1999, כ-25,000 פליטים אלבנים שהו במחנה המעבר ברזדה בסטנקובץ.
claims.quote: Muharemi is one of the estimated 25,000 ethnic Albanian refugees from Kosovo now in the Brazda refugee transit camp, which was established last week at the Stenkovec airfield

claims.text: במחנה סטנקובץ הגיעו מדי יום אוטובוסים של אלבנים רעבים וטראומטיים, ותור האוכל מנה תמיד מאות.
claims.quote: At the Stenkovec camp, busloads of hungry, traumatized Albanians arrive daily. The food line is never less than hundreds deep.

claims.text: במחנה לא היו שירותים ניידים אלא קרשי עץ מנוקבים מעל בורות, וריח של צואה אדם עמד באוויר.
claims.quote: there are no portable toilets, only holed-out wood planks across large pits; the scent of human waste pervades the camp.

claims.text: פליטים שרואיינו ב-RFE/RL הביעו שביעות רצון מהשירותים בברזדה; התלונות העיקריות היו מחסור במקלחות ושעמום.
claims.quote: Refugees interviewed by RFE/RL expressed satisfaction with the services offered in Brazda. The main complaints are a lack of showers and of boredom.

claims.text: סטודנטית לכלכלה מפריסטינה, בת 22, התלוננה בחריפות שבמחנה חיים "כמו חיות".
claims.quote: At the start of the 21st century, we are living like animals here. It is so bad.

claims.text: הרופא דן אנגלהרד, פרופסור בהדסה, צפה שעם עליית הטמפרטורות יפרצו מגפות כמו חצבת, פוליו ודיזנטריה.
claims.quote: But as the temperature warms, there will likely be epidemics such as measles, polio and dysentery, said pediatrician Engelhard, a professor at Hadassah-Hebrew University Medical Center in Jerusalem.

claims.text: לדברי אנגלהרד, גורמים מקדונים וארגוני סיוע התעכבו באספקת תברואה וחיסונים, והילדים חשופים במיוחד.
claims.quote: Macedonian officials and relief agencies have been slow to provide good sanitation and immunization; without it, children in particular are vulnerable to diarrhea, vomiting, and skin infections, he said.

claims.text: אנגלהרד, רופא ילדים ומילואימניק שכבר שירת בבתי חולים שדה ישראליים בקמבודיה וברואנדה, אמר שאי אפשר להשוות את קוסובו לשואה, אך התמונות של אלבנים מגורשים לרכבות מזכירות אותה.
claims.quote: But you can’t compare this with the Holocaust. No way. The Nazis tried to kill every Jew. However, when we see these pictures of Albanians forced out of their homes and into trains, it certainly reminds us of the Holocaust.

claims.text: מאור אמר שהפליטים "בני מזל" יותר מסביו וסבתו בפולין ובהונגריה בזמן המלחמה, כי לאלבנים יש מאמץ בינלאומי לעזור להם.
claims.quote: “These refugees are luckier than my grandparents were in Poland and Hungary during the war,” said Maor, the army surgeon.

claims.text: לפי UNHCR, ביום שני 12 באפריל 1999 פונו במסגרת תוכנית פינוי הומניטרית כ-1,300 פליטים ממקדוניה לגרמניה, ישראל, נורווגיה וטורקיה; הפליטים שפונו לישראל היו בעיקר מקרים רפואיים מיוחדים שטופלו תחילה בבית החולים השדה הישראלי בברזדה.
claims.quote: The refugees evacuated to Israel were mainly special medical cases who were treated initially in the Israeli field hospital in Brazda camp.

claims.text: לוי אמר ב-14 באפריל שישראל שלחה באותו יום כ-100 פליטים במטוס לישראל, ושלדעתו המחנה יפעל לפחות כמה שבועות.
claims.quote: we've also sent about 100 refugees today to Israel by aircraft. Israel was willing to accept them. So it's my guess it's going to last a few weeks, at least until there is any solution.

claims.text: שני פליטים מקוסובו קיבלו אישור לטוס לישראל עם הצוות, כחלק מקבוצה של 111 פליטים אלבנים שהגיעה לישראל שבוע קודם.
claims.quote: who had received permission to join a group of 111 ethnic Albanian refugees who arrived in Israel last week.

claims.text: המנדט הישראלי של שבועיים עמד לפוג, והצוות היה צפוי לעזוב ביום חמישי.
claims.quote: Their two-week mandate expires soon, and they were expected to ship out Thursday.

claims.text: אנשי הצוות אמרו שהם רוצים להישאר באתר עד שיגיעו צוותי החלפה ממדינות אחרות.
claims.quote: said they want to remain at the site until replacement teams arrived from other countries.

claims.text: בית חולים שדה של צבא ישראל במקדוניה דחה את חזרתו לישראל מיום שני ליום חמישי.
claims.quote: An Israeli army field hospital operating in Macedonia postponed its return to Israel from Monday to Thursday.

claims.text: מתקן רפואי שני, של הצלב האדום הגרמני, הוקם בתוך שבוע אחרי בית החולים הישראלי.
claims.quote: A second medical facility followed within a week, operated by the German Red Cross.

claims.text: את הטיפול בבית החולים עמדו להעביר הגרמנים וצוות שהגיע מטייוואן.
claims.quote: the Germans and a newly arrived team from Taiwan will take over hospital care.

claims.text: לפי JTA, בית החולים הוקם במחנה הפליטים ברזדה ב-6 באפריל כדי לתת שירותים רפואיים לאלבנים אתניים שנמלטו מקוסובו.
claims.quote: which was set up in the Brazde refugee camp on April 6 to provide medical services for ethnic Albanians fleeing Kosovo

claims.text: בכתבת RFE/RL מ-14 באפריל סיפר אל"ם לוי שישראל שלחה כ-100 פליטים במטוס לישראל; לפי UNHCR, הפינוי לישראל נערך ביום שני, 12 באפריל.
claims.quote: On Monday UNHCR coordinated the evacuation of just over 1,300 refugees from Macedonia to Germany, Israel, Norway and Turkey.
